clinician.trajectory_summary: A 62-year-old male with diabetes, hypertension, and coronary artery disease presented to the ED with a 4-month history of 25-pound unintentional weight loss and 4 days of persistent hiccups. On admission, he was febrile (38.4°C) and mildly tachycardic (HR 104 bpm). Chest X-ray revealed new groundglass opacities in the right upper lung, left mid and lower lungs, and right costophrenic angle, consistent with pneumonia. Laboratory studies showed leukopenia (4,200 cells/μL), thrombocytopenia (15,000 platelets/μL), hyponatremia (131 mEq/L), and hypochloremia (98 mEq/L). The patient was placed in isolation as a person under investigation and empirically treated with ceftriaxone 1 g IV and azithromycin 500 mg IV for possible pneumonia. A COVID-19 swab and respiratory viral panel were sent on admission. He was admitted to the COVID medical unit and discharged 3 days after admission in stable condition with symptomatic care.
